cards.when: a balanced DMU×period panel with inputs (K,L,materials) & outputs (GDP); non-parametric TFP: malm=change, fareprim=levels (multilateral transitive)
cards.when_not: a single time series for one DMU; an unbalanced panel; parametric/SFA with noise; decomposition of forecast variance (→ FEVD, cat. 04)

alternatives.criterion: you want comparable TFP LEVELS across many DMU/years at once (multilateral); the only transitive+complete index (O'Donnell 2012)
you want the CHANGE in TFP between adjacent periods (Solow-style, quantity-only, effch×tech)
you want to separate inefficiency from random noise (DEA attributes everything to inefficiency) and you accept a functional form
excluded (charter §4): non-transitive or price-based, redundant next to malm+fareprim

output_key_fields: Changes.malmquist: the TFP change index; >1=improvement, <1=deterioration (the same under both orientations)
Changes.effch: efficiency change (catching up to the frontier); malmquist=effch×tech
Changes.tech: technological change (a shift of the frontier); obtech/ibtech/matech are its components
TFP in Levels (prod_fare_primont): the TFP level, transitive → directly comparable across units and periods
TFPE = TFP/MP ∈ (0,1] in Levels; OTE/OSE/OME: technical/scale/mix efficiency (output-oriented)
REV/COST/PROF in Levels: profitability, ONLY when prices are supplied (w_vars/p_vars)
Changes (prod_fare_primont): the changes are prefixed with 'd' (dTFP, dOTE, dPROF); Shadowp only when shadow=True
interpretation_traps: efficiency scores ∈(0,1]; a value=1 = best-in-sample frontier, NOT absolutely perfect (DEA is relative/deterministic)
zero/negative inputs/outputs → SILENT garbage (a zero output → malmquist ~1e30); the gate requires strictly >0
a categorical time variable → DEA sorts by category order rather than chronologically → a SILENTLY sign-flipped TFP change
the Levels/Changes/Shadowp accessors are unreliable; read the Levels and Changes blocks directly
DEA has no noise term: outliers/measurement error shift the frontier & distort every score
an unbalanced panel is not supported; prod_malmquist needs >=2 periods, prod_fare_primont >=1
sources: Färe & Grosskopf 1996 Intertemporal Production Frontiers (Malmquist decomposition)

cards.when: cross-section; decomposing the MEAN gap of a continuous outcome between TWO groups (0/1) into explained/endowments vs unexplained/coefficients (+interaction, three-fold)
cards.when_not: >2 groups; a causal claim (unexplained ≠ discrimination); a non-linear/binary outcome; a time-series/panel gap

alternatives.criterion: you want an explicit interaction term + a complete accounting split with no reference choice (Jann 2008)
you want 'how much of the gap closes if we equalised X'; choose group_weight (pooled or A/B)
the gap varies across the DISTRIBUTION (glass ceiling/sticky floor), not only at the mean
a binary or count outcome; outside this wrapper (the regression function is locked to least squares)

output_key_fields: twofold: overall per reference weight (group_weight); coef_explained/se_explained (endowments), coef_unexplained/se_unexplained (+_A/_B)
twofold_variables: the decomposition per regressor (column variable)
threefold: coef_endowments, coef_coefficients, coef_interaction (+SEs)
threefold_variables: three-fold per regressor
x_means: mean_A/mean_B/mean_diff per regressor (the raw material of the endowments effect)
y: y_A/y_B/y_diff — mean outcomes & the total gap (= the sum of the components)
n: n_A/n_B/n_pooled; n_dropped: the rows silently dropped for missing values
interpretation_traps: an invalid group, input or formula makes the decomposition emit a message and return nothing at all rather than raising — hence a pre-gate and a post-gate that the result is non-empty
a degenerate fit: a per-group least-squares fit that is rank-deficient or has df_residual<=0 comes back with misleading coefficients and NO error; hence a post-gate on each group regression
'unexplained' ≠ discrimination: it absorbs omitted variables & functional-form error (Jann 2008); NOT causal
sign: y_diff=y_A−y_B (group=0 → A); check which group is 0/1 before interpreting; the components sum to y_diff
the two-fold split depends on the reference group_weight; a different weight → a different explained/unexplained split
the bootstrap standard errors are stochastic → the generator is seeded before the call (the same seed → an identical split)
rows with missing values are dropped silently → n_dropped reports them
sources: Blinder 1973 J. Human Resources; Oaxaca 1973 Int. Economic Review (the original decompositions)
Jann 2008 Stata Journal 8(4):453-479 (two-fold reference schemes, three-fold, unexplained≠discrimination)

cards.method: Price index numbers (bilateral/multilateral/spliced) + CPI-subindex contribution decompositions
cards.when: long-format scanner/CPI micro data (time,prices,quantities,prodID); you want a price index (bilateral or multilateral) or a decomposition of the change in the value of a CPI subindex into price/quantity contributions per product
cards.when_not: you already have a finished index-level series (an index level ts) — that is a transform/growth-rate task, not index-number construction; a macro aggregate without product-level micro data; a need for SPQ/model-based or chained bilateral batch indices (outside the curated surface)

alternatives.criterion: high product turnover / new-goods bias — the bilateral indices (Laspeyres/Paasche) suffer chain drift; you want a transitive multilateral index
you want a non-revisable extending multilateral series beyond a fixed window (a rolling-window splice)
you want a TFP/quantity index (Färe-Primont) rather than a price index

output_key_fields: pi_bilateral: index (a scalar, or a vector when interval=True); formula; dates (the month labels when an interval is used)
pi_multilateral: index (a scalar, end vs start over the window); method; window; wstart
pi_splice: index (a scalar, or the full series when interval=True); method; splice; dates
aggregate (pi_contributions): one row {Value_difference, Price_indicator, Quantity_indicator} — the identity value = price + quantity
contributions (pi_contributions): a per-product frame {prodID, value_differences, price_contributions, quantity_contributions}; plus n_products
interpretation_traps: start > end SILENTLY returns a wrong, inverted index — the wrapper blocks it with a gate; always keep start <= end
bilateral Laspeyres/Paasche over/understate because of substitution bias; Fisher/Törnqvist (superlative) is the correct baseline; a large Laspeyres–Paasche gap => move to multilateral
gk = Geary-Khamis rolling window (the default here); it differs from geary_khamis (fixed base, not exposed); do not confuse them
window (multilateral/splice): an integer >= 2 months; too small a window => noise, too large => the composition becomes out of date
pi_contributions: the price_contributions of a product can be 0 when its price did not change — the quantity is a contribution to the value DIFFERENCE (an indicator, not an index ratio)
interval=False gives a single index, end against start (with the base at start = 1); interval=True gives a dated series for a chart
sources: ILO/IMF/OECD/Eurostat/UNECE/World Bank (2004, 2020) Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice
Diewert (1976) Exact and superlative index numbers, J. Econometrics 4:115
Bennet (1920) The theory of measurement of changes in cost of living, JRSS 83:455; Montgomery (1937)
Krsinich (2016) The FEWS index: Fixed Effects with a Window Splice (UNECE-ILO); de Haan & Krsinich (2014) multilateral GEKS
precondition_tools: pi_bilateral (the bilateral baseline; check the Laspeyres vs Paasche drift before choosing multilateral)
pi_multilateral (GEKS/CCDI/GK/TPD; a transitive base for splicing)

cards.method: Growth accounting and Tornqvist-Divisia total factor productivity
cards.when: splitting output growth into contributions from measured inputs and the residual, which is the standard framing for productivity analysis
cards.when_not: the input shares are unavailable; the residual would absorb so much that it explains nothing

alternatives.criterion: shares are stable
shares move and you want a superlative index
you want elasticities rather than shares

output_key_fields: tfp_growth: the residual
contributions: growth attributed to each input
shares: the factor shares used, period by period
index: the Tornqvist or Divisia index level
interpretation_traps: THE SOLOW RESIDUAL IS A RESIDUAL: it absorbs measurement error, capacity utilisation, markups and mismeasured input quality, and calling it technology is an interpretation
using fixed shares when shares actually move introduces a substitution bias that the Tornqvist index exists to remove
capital services and the capital stock are different concepts; using the stock understates input growth

cards.when: separating inefficiency from noise when measuring how far a unit is from best practice, which a simple residual cannot do
cards.when_not: there is no reason to expect one-sided inefficiency; the sample is too small to identify the two error components

alternatives.criterion: you want a deterministic, non-parametric frontier
noise must be separated from inefficiency
efficiency is not the question

output_key_fields: params: frontier coefficients
efficiency: per-unit technical efficiency scores
lambda_: ratio of inefficiency to noise variance -- the identification diagnostic
one_sided_test: test that inefficiency is present at all
interpretation_traps: IF LAMBDA IS NEAR ZERO THE INEFFICIENCY COMPONENT IS NOT IDENTIFIED and the efficiency scores are noise dressed as estimates
the test of no inefficiency sits on the boundary of the parameter space, so the naive p-value is wrong and a mixture distribution is required
efficiency scores depend on the assumed inefficiency distribution -- half-normal, truncated normal, exponential -- and rankings change with it

cards.method: Data envelopment analysis with scale and technical decomposition
cards.when: measuring efficiency against a deterministic best-practice frontier built from the data, with no functional form assumed
cards.when_not: the data contain material noise, which DEA attributes entirely to inefficiency; the sample is small relative to the number of inputs and outputs

alternatives.criterion: noise must be separated
scale efficiency is not of interest
you want to separate pure technical from scale efficiency

output_key_fields: efficiency: per-unit scores
technical, scale: the decomposition under variable returns
peers: the reference units defining each unit's frontier segment
returns_to_scale: increasing, constant or decreasing per unit
interpretation_traps: DEA ATTRIBUTES ALL DEVIATION TO INEFFICIENCY; a single mismeasured unit can shift the frontier and change every other unit's score
with many inputs and outputs relative to units, almost everything is efficient by construction -- the dimensionality rule of thumb is not optional
scores are relative to the sample, so adding or removing units changes them
sources: Charnes, Cooper & Rhodes 1978 (European Journal of Operational Research 2:429-444)

cards.method: Multilateral and scanner-data price indices: GEKS and time-product dummy
cards.when: high-frequency scanner data where products enter and leave constantly, and a bilateral index chains drift badly
cards.when_not: the product set is stable, where a bilateral index is fine; the data have no expenditure weights

alternatives.criterion: stable product set
multilateral, transitive by construction
a regression-based multilateral index

output_key_fields: index: the price index series
method: which multilateral form produced it
window: the estimation window and the splicing method
churn: product entry and exit rates, which motivate the method
interpretation_traps: CHAIN DRIFT is the problem these methods solve: a bilateral chained index over high-frequency scanner data can drift by tens of percent with no underlying price change
multilateral indices must be extended over time by splicing, and the splicing choice -- movement, window, mean -- changes the series
the estimation window length trades transitivity against responsiveness and is a substantive choice
sources: de Haan & Krsinich 2014 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 32:341)

cards.when: splitting a region's growth into what national growth, its industry mix and its own competitiveness contributed
cards.when_not: the industry classification is inconsistent over the period; there is no national benchmark to compare against

alternatives.criterion: the standard decomposition
weights update over time
you want an instrument rather than a decomposition

output_key_fields: national, industry_mix, competitive: the three contributions
total: the sum, which must equal observed regional growth
by_industry: contributions per industry
residual: zero by construction in the classic form
interpretation_traps: THE COMPETITIVE COMPONENT IS A RESIDUAL and absorbs everything the classification does not capture -- it is not a measure of competitiveness in any causal sense
the decomposition is sensitive to the level of industry aggregation; finer classifications shift variation from competitive to industry mix
using shift-share as an instrument requires an entirely separate exogeneity argument about the initial shares
sources: Dunn 1960 (Papers of the Regional Science Association 6:97-112)

cards.when: decomposing a gap between two distributions into what composition explains and what returns explain, at any quantile rather than just the mean
cards.when_not: the two groups have no common support in covariates; only the mean gap matters and a simple decomposition suffices

alternatives.criterion: mean gaps only
distributional gaps, no functional form
you want detailed contributions per covariate at a quantile

output_key_fields: composition, structure: the two components at each quantile
detailed: per-covariate contributions, where RIF is used
common_support: units dropped for lack of overlap
reweighting_factors: the DFL weights
interpretation_traps: THE DETAILED DECOMPOSITION DEPENDS ON THE OMITTED CATEGORY of every categorical variable; the aggregate split does not, but the per-covariate numbers do
reweighting requires common support; without it the counterfactual distribution is an extrapolation
RIF regressions are a local approximation and can be poor away from the evaluated quantile
sources: Fortin, Lemieux & Firpo 2011 (Handbook of Labor Economics 4A)

cards.method: Structural decomposition analysis of input-output tables
cards.when: attributing a change in output, emissions or value added to changes in technology, final demand structure and demand level, through the supply chain
cards.when_not: you only have aggregate factors (-> index decomposition); the tables are not comparable between the two periods

alternatives.criterion: aggregate factors only, no supply chain
input-output tables for both periods
partial table detail

output_key_fields: contributions: change attributed to technology, demand structure and demand level
residual: interaction terms not attributed
decomposition_form: which of the many equivalent forms was used
by_sector: sectoral detail of each contribution
interpretation_traps: THERE ARE MANY EQUIVALENT DECOMPOSITION FORMS and they give different answers; the convention is to average over polar forms, and the form used must be stated
the two tables must be in constant prices and on the same classification, or the decomposition attributes price and classification changes to technology
the number of decomposition terms grows factorially with the number of factors, which is why averaging is used
